source_anchor: Theorem 1, Section 3.2; proof in Appendix A
statement: For every multivariate square-integrable f on [-pi,pi]^d with values in [0,1] and every epsilon > 0, some SAQNN parameters theta, phi and positive rescale a achieve L2 error at most epsilon.

assumptions.output: a times the square root of the O measurement probability

proof_obligations: Trigonometric polynomials are dense in L2 on the d-torus.
State preparation and phase injection encode every finite complex coefficient vector after positive l1 rescaling.
Spectrum selection realizes exp(i j dot x) for every selected integer frequency.
The measured square-root output equals the magnitude of the selected polynomial.
For f >= 0, pointwise ||g|-f| <= |g-f|, hence the L2 error cannot increase.
